pl-l4d2c6-d1e115.summary: Asks whether those baptized by John were baptized again with Christ's baptism, and what form of words John used.

pl-l4d2c6-d1e118.summary: States that those baptized by John who did not know there was a Holy Spirit and put their hope in his baptism were afterward baptized with Christ's baptism. John's baptism was given in the name of the one to come.
claims: Those who hoped in John's baptism and did not know the Spirit received Christ's baptism.
John baptized in the name of the one to come.

pl-l4d2c6-d1e121.summary: Quotes Jerome on Joel: one who says he believes in Christ and does not believe in the Holy Spirit does not yet see clearly. So those baptized by John in the name of the one to come, the Lord Jesus, who said 'we have not heard whether there is a Holy Spirit', were baptized again, or rather received true baptism.
claims: Those baptized by John without knowing the Spirit received true baptism afterward.

pl-l4d2c6-d1e131.summary: States that those who did not put their hope in John's baptism and believed in Father, Son, and Holy Spirit were not baptized afterward, but received the Holy Spirit through the apostles' laying on of hands; the others were baptized with Christ's baptism.
claims: Those baptized by John who believed in the Trinity received the Spirit by laying on of hands.

pl-l4d2c6-d1e134.summary: Quotes Jerome: those who did not know the Holy Spirit when they received John's baptism were baptized again, so that no Jew or gentile would think water without the Holy Spirit could suffice for salvation.
claims: Water without the Spirit does not suffice for salvation.

pl-l4d2c6-d1e143.summary: Quotes Ambrose: some denied knowing the Holy Spirit though baptized with John's baptism, which was in the name of the coming Jesus, not John's own. Since they were baptized neither in Christ's name nor with faith in the Spirit, they could not receive the sacrament of baptism; so they were baptized in Christ's name, and baptism was not repeated in them but renewed.
claims: Those baptized by John without faith in the Spirit had not received the sacrament of baptism.
Their baptism in Christ's name was not a repetition.

pl-l4d2c6.summary: Asks whether those baptized by John were baptized again with Christ's baptism, and with what form of words John baptized. Those baptized by John who did not know of the Holy Spirit and put their hope in his baptism were later baptized with Christ's; John baptized in the name of the one to come. Jerome says those who said they had not heard of the Holy Spirit were rebaptized, indeed received true baptism, so no one would think water sufficient without the Spirit. Those who did not hope in John's baptism and believed in Father, Son, and Spirit were not rebaptized but received the Spirit by the apostles' laying on of hands. Ambrose says baptism was not repeated in them but renewed.
claims: John baptized in the name of the one to come.
Those baptized by John who did not know the Spirit received Christ's baptism.
Those who believed in the Trinity received the Spirit by the laying on of hands.
Christ's baptism after John's was not a repetition but true baptism.
